notes: Plan-only evals, graded offline against expected_output like ship-release's — ship-issue's phases push, open PRs, and merge, so exercising them for real would need a throwaway GitHub repo rather than a local fixture. Each prompt therefore says plan-only and asks for the command sequence. The prompts assume a GitHub remote with `gh` available; evals 1 and 2 assume integrationBranch == defaultBranch, eval 3 deliberately sets them apart. `run-eval.sh ship-issue <id>` prints the prompt and the expected output for manual or CI grading.

evals.name: phase-walk-with-no-improvised-polling
evals.prompt:
This worktree is finished — implementation is committed and I want it landed. **Plan-only: don't push, don't open a PR, don't merge anything.** Walk me through every phase in order with the exact commands you'd run.

Be specific about how you wait for CI. I've been burned by agents that sit there re-running `gh pr checks | grep` in a loop, or firing off `date`/`true` to pass the time, and burn my whole budget before the build even finishes. Tell me the exact wait command, whether it runs in the foreground or the background, and what you do when it times out.
evals.expected_output: An ordered walk of phases 0-8 with real commands. The CI answer is the load-bearing part: exactly one blocking call, `timeout 300 gh pr checks <pr-num> --watch --fail-fast --interval 30`, run in the **foreground** — explicitly not backgrounded and not waited on with Monitor, because the harness yields a subagent indefinitely on a long-running monitored background Bash. On exit 124 it emits one short narration turn as a keep-alive and re-runs the same command, up to 8 times (~40 min), then escalates with the documented options (wait, close+reopen, admin-merge, abort). It must explicitly reject the improvised alternatives the prompt names: no bare `gh pr checks` polling loop, no repeated `gh run view`/`tail`, no no-op keep-alive commands — each is a full model turn that re-reads the session prefix. Before blocking it re-checks `gh pr view <pr-num> --json headRefOid` against the reviewed `HEAD_SHA` — the value fixed at Phase 5 and re-fixed each time a fix push lands — never against a freshly-read `git rev-parse HEAD`, which in a shared checkout already carries another attempt's commits. Divergence means unreviewed commits on the branch: it stops before the CI wait and the merge rather than re-pushing. Surrounding phases should be recognisable and not invented: pre-flight (linked worktree via git-common-dir vs git-dir, branch matches the configured pattern with the optional worktree prefix, clean `git status --porcelain`, no open PR); Phase 1 fetch + merge `origin/<integrationBranch>` into the feature branch with the auto-resolve allowlist for lockfiles/migrations/generated files/.claude/settings.json and escalation for everything else, plus the divergence rule (a worktree-driven merge proceeds even in --auto; anything that would rewrite the local integration branch stops regardless); Phase 2 verify commands resolved from config with the environmental-vs-real baseline for test failures; Phase 3 reading CONSOLIDATE.md rather than paraphrasing consolidation from memory; Phase 4 runs `check-launch` (SKILL.md's `## Launch guard`) immediately before `git push -u`, and `check-launch` again immediately before `gh pr create --base <integrationBranch>` with the `Closes #<num>` trailer, stopping without performing that write on anything but `current: true`; Phase 5 the degradation decision — merge-delta-only check when review_state is clean, the sync was conflict-free, and the diff is small (≤1,000 product lines / ≤20 product files, measured with `diff-scope` rather than hand-counted numstat arithmetic); the full two-axis review (conformance ∥ correctness, never merged) whenever any degradation prerequisite fails (review_state residuals or unknown, manual conflict escalations, oversized diff) or on the risky label / criticalPaths hits; Phase 7 `gh pr merge --merge` with no `--no-ff` (gh rejects it); Phase 8 issue-close verification and worktree removal from the main root. `unset GITHUB_TOKEN` appears only if the project config sets unsetGithubToken.

evals.name: apply-vs-push-discipline
evals.prompt:
The reviewer subagent came back on my PR with two Blocking findings and one Should-fix. I'm running this in auto mode (`from-issue --auto` dispatched you).

Before you touch anything: write out the exact order of operations you'll follow, from "I have review findings" to "CI is running on the fixed code". I want the steps, not the edits — **don't modify or push anything yet.** Tell me what specifically goes wrong if the order slips.
evals.expected_output: The five-step Phase 5 order, kept as five distinct steps rather than collapsed into 'fix and push': (1) edit the file(s); (2) re-run the configured lint and test commands against the modified surface; (3) `git add` the changed files and commit as `fix(issue-<num>): address PR review — <short blocker>`, honouring commit.coAuthoredBy; (4) `git push`; (5) verify the push landed by comparing `gh pr view <pr-num> --json headRefOid` to `git rev-parse HEAD`, and if they diverge, re-push before continuing; once they match, re-fix `HEAD_SHA` to that observed `headRefOid`. It must name the concrete failure mode the ordering exists to prevent: edited files, ran tests, forgot to commit, then advanced to Phase 6 and polled CI on the stale tip — so CI goes green on the unfixed code. Phase 6 then compares `headRefOid` to the reviewed `HEAD_SHA` before blocking on the watch — a different comparand, not a repeat of clause (5). On auto mode: the Should-fix gets the same five steps plus a PR comment carrying a one-line rationale; only Discussion items are surfaced to the user, with a doc-grounded prompt. A response that merges apply-and-push into one verb, skips the headRefOid check, or treats Should-fix items as user-facing in auto mode is a failure.

evals.name: auto-close-when-integration-branch-is-not-default
evals.prompt:
Heads up on our branching: features merge into `dev`, and `dev` only goes to `main` at release time. `main` is the repo's default branch on GitHub.

Ship issue #142 from this worktree. **Plan-only for now** — no push, no PR, no merge. One thing I want you to be explicit about: how does issue #142 actually get closed, and at which step? Last time an issue sat open for a week after its PR had already merged.
evals.expected_output: The answer must turn on integrationBranch (`dev`) not equalling defaultBranch (`main`). GitHub's auto-close-on-merge fires only when the PR's base is the repository default branch, so merging this PR into `dev` will **not** close #142 — that is precisely the week-long-open bug the user described. The `Closes #142` trailer still belongs in the PR body for the UI linkage and traceability, but it is not the close mechanism here and the plan must say so rather than relying on it. The real close is Phase 8 step 1, run explicitly after the merge is verified: `gh issue view 142 --json state`, and when it comes back OPEN, `gh issue close 142`. The PR is opened with `gh pr create --base dev`. Failures: claiming the merge will auto-close the issue; proposing to retarget the PR at `main` to get auto-close; dropping the `Closes` trailer entirely; or listing `gh issue close` as optional cleanup rather than the mechanism. A good answer also notes that other issue/PR references in the body and comments use full URLs rather than bare `#N`, with the `Closes #<num>` trailer as the one sanctioned exception.
